title: MEAL Officer
description:
Location: Ethiopia, India, Italy, Jordan, Kenya (as long as HelpAge International holds the registration in this country), Nepal, Pakistan, Spain, Tanzania, Thailand, Turkey, United Kingdom and Zimbabwe Department: Global Impact Reports to (Line Manager): Global Impact Advisor Grade: C Contract Type: Open-ended contract About HelpAge HelpAge International works with a diverse global network of around 200 organisations across 99 countries to promote the rights of older people to lead dignified, healthy and secure lives. Through partnership and collaborations, we work to ensure the inclusion of older people across society and strive to deliver a just and fair world for everyone as they get older. Our work is driven by our desire to achieve real impact for older people, to be inclusive, to work in partnership and to learn from our shared experience. About the Job The MEAL Officer plays a critical role in enhancing the quality, effectiveness, and accountability of HelpAge’s global programmes, advocacy efforts, and organizational performance. This role coordinates and provides technical input into the design and implementation of monitoring and evaluation (M&E) frameworks, supports learning processes, and provides technical advice to teams and Network Members. The postholder will work collaboratively across teams and Impact Vehicles to coordinates performance measurement, evaluations, rapid needs assessments and key planning and reporting processes, ensuring that HelpAge’s programmes and influencing initiatives are grounded in evidence, informed by the voices of older people, and contribute to a strong culture of learning, transparency, and continuous improvement. Key areas for impact/influence and responsibilities 1. Organisational Performance and Monitoring and Evaluation Frameworks Coordinate and provide technical input into the development and implementation of robust M&E frameworks and tools for global programmes, advocacy initiatives, and Impact Vehicles. Support Impact Vehicle, cross-functional, and programmes teams in defining indicators, setting baselines, and tracking outcomes aligned to HelpAge’s Global Impact Framework. Coordinate the development and review of results frameworks, log frames, indicators, baselines, and targets across teams and Impact Vehicles. Lead the identification and development of appropriate data sources, data-collection methodologies and evidence requirements for organisational and Impact Vehicle indicators and targets. Act as the organisational focal point for standardising KPI measurement across all Impact Vehicles, establishing and maintaining consistent indicator definitions, measurement tools, evidence requirements and reporting approaches, subject to final technical sign-off by the Global Impact Adviser. Coordinate organisation-wide Impact Vehicle performance tracking, working with relevant teams to ensure the timely and consistent collection, analysis and reporting of results. Coordinate and undertake the drafting and revision of organisational MEAL policies, procedures, standards and guidance. 2. Technical MEL Support for Global Impact Team Provide advanced technical MEAL advice, support, and quality assurance across HelpAge’s global programme portfolio, working with programme teams and Network Members throughout proposal development, programme design, implementation, monitoring, reporting and learning. Provide technical support to advocacy teams to track and measure the outcomes and influence of campaigns, policy engagement, and strategic partnerships. Develop and apply methodologies and tools for monitoring policy change, stakeholder influence, and advocacy impact. 3. Accountability and Participation Provide guidance on participatory monitoring approaches, ensuring meaningful inclusion of older people and marginalised groups. Work with programme and network member teams to build inclusive, culturally appropriate feedback and response systems at community or country level. Collaborate with the Data and Accountability Officer to ensure feedback data is analysed and used to inform adaptive programming and advocacy refinement. Promote transparency, responsiveness, and power-sharing through strengthened accountability practices. 4. Organisational Learning and Knowledge Sharing Coordinate learning reviews, after-action reviews, and annual and mid-term reflection processes within and across teams. Document and disseminate key learning, good practices, and innovations. Facilitate cross-organisational learning events, webinars, and communities of practice. 5. Rapid Needs Assessments Act as HelpAge’s technical focal point for rapid needs assessments, establishing and maintaining organisational methodologies, tools, standards and guidance.Advise and coordinate teams undertaking rapid needs assessments, determining appropriate sampling approaches, data-collection methods, questionnaire design, analytical process, and quality-assurance requirements Undertake the coordination and final technical quality assurance of rapid needs assessment reports, including establishing requirements and timelines, coordinating and consolidating inputs from colleagues, and ensuring that findings and recommendations are methodologically robust, supported by the available evidence and suitable for organisational or external use. 6. Evaluation and Evidence Generation Act as a technical focal point for evaluations of short-term projects, advising teams on appropriate evaluation approaches, methodology and design, and coordinating evaluations as required, with overall organisational technical oversight remaining with the Global Impact Adviser. Provide technical quality assurance on evaluation design, methodology, findings, and deliverables. Support the development of evaluation terms of reference and methodologies, and support the process, from inception, data collection, analysis and delivery. Coordinate the dissemination of evaluation findings across the organisation, and support teams to use findings to influence strategy, fundraising, and programme design. Capacity Strengthening Design and deliver training and tailored support to HelpAge teams, partners, and network members on MEL and accountability. Develop user-friendly guidance, templates, and toolkits to strengthen MEL practices across the organisation. Build internal capacity for adaptive management and evidence use in decision-making. 7. Planning, Reporting, and Coordination Support the Global Impact Adviser by coordinating key components of HelpAge’s annual business planning, organisational and donor reporting cycles, including coordinating and reviewing inputs from teams across functions and regions. Work closely with the Global Impact Advisor and Data and Accountability Officer to ensure effective data use and alignment of organizational planning and reporting, systems, data use, and frameworks. Actively participate in the relevant cross-team learning and coordination platforms. Contribute MEL insights to fundraising, donor reporting, and strategic planning processes. Skills and experience required Essential Significant experience in Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning in international development, humanitarian, or advocacy-focused organisations. Advanced knowledge of MEAL principles, demonstrated by experience designing M&E frameworks, theories of change, indicators, and MEL plans. Strong technical skills in both quantitative and qualitative data collection and analysis. Experience applying MEL in advocacy, campaigning, or policy-influencing settings. Experience coordinating donor or organisational reporting and translating complex programme and performance information into clear, evidence-based narratives. Experience coordinating organisation-wide or multi-team planning, performance measurement or reporting processes, including setting requirements, managing inputs and challenging incomplete or poor-quality submissions. Knowledge of accountability principles and practical experience with feedback, complaints, and response mechanisms. Strong facilitation skills and experience designing and delivering MEAL training and learning events. Ability to communicate technical information clearly to non-specialist audiences. Proven ability to work collaboratively across diverse teams and cultural contexts. Familiarity with digital data collection and analysis tools (e.g., Power BI, Kobo Toolbox, DHIS2, Excel). Demonstrated experience coordinating rapid needs assessments in humanitarian contexts, including developing methodologies and tools, directing technical inputs, addressing data-quality and analytical issues, coordinating report production, and providing final technical quality assurance. Excellent written and spoken English, including the ability to produce and quality assure high-quality organisational and donor reports. Flexibility to work across different time zones. Demonstrated understanding of and a commitment to the principles of Partner Led Programming is essential. Desirable Excellent communication skills in English (spoken and written); Fluency in one or more additional languages used in the Global South (e.g., Spanish, French, Arabic) are highly desirable. Ability to work across cultures, sectors, and geographies in inclusive and equitable ways. Knowledge of ageing, disability, inclusion, humanitarian inclusion, or rights-based programming. Key Behavioural Competencies Working Collaboratively with Others: Work collaboratively, building mutual trust and respect, with external organizations and partners to achieve our strategic aims and objectives; being accountable for the work we do together. Adaptability and Flexibility: Adapt to new directions or opportunities arising within the organisation and in our work area; being flexible in our role, constantly using the feedback to learn more and evolve further. Supporting and Facilitating Change: Lead behavioural and cultural change through embracing a supportive, collaborative and highly inclusive environment where everybody feels supported, respected and engaged. Extend HelpAge’s Reach and Impact: Extend HelpAge’s reach and impact by creating and identifying new business development opportunities and building relationships with new partners. Diversity and Inclusion: Lead and promote a culture of including the voices of older people across our support, convening and thought leadership roles, in a way that is transformative, empowering and highly inclusive of those marginalised by gender, economic status, disability and other factors of discrimination. Leading Others(for managers): Demonstrate strong leadership to own unit/department and manage people in a well and reputable manner. Create an atmosphere of trust and an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential. Safeguarding HelpAge International is committed to safeguarding the communities with which we work, our partners, staff and any others who we come into contact with. The post holder will also be responsible for: Preventing harm and abuse from our people, operations and programmes to anyone that encounters our work. Reporting all safeguarding incidents you see, hear, hear about or suspect, using our internal reporting mechanism. Complying with all safeguarding framework policies and practices. Completing mandatory training courses relating to our safeguarding policy framework and complying with HR vetting procedures. SAFER RECRUITMENT All employments at HelpAge International will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include misconduct disclosure schemes and terrorism finance checks.

How to Apply: Qualified and experienced candidates are encouraged to review the full Job Description and submit their **Cover Letter and CV** to **Jobs@helpage.org** no later than **Tuesday,** **13 October 2026**. Applicants must have the legal right to live and work in the stated locations. Please note that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

title: Regional Finance Controller - Kenya
description:
Location: Nairobi, Kenya (for exceptional candidates, we are open to other countries where IRW has a country office in the African region) Contract: Permanent Salary: £38,322 Closing Date: 11th October 2026 Islamic Relief Worldwide (IRW) is a faith-based humanitarian and development organisation working to save and transform the lives of some of the world's most vulnerable people. Established in 1984 and operating in over 45 countries, we respond to emergencies, tackle poverty, empower communities, and advocate for lasting change. We are seeking an experienced and strategic Regional Finance Controller - Africa (West and East) to join our Finance & Corporate Services Division. This is a unique opportunity for a senior finance leader who is passionate about financial governance, capacity building, compliance, and driving sustainable improvement across complex international operations. The preferred location for this role is Nairobi, Kenya. However, we recognise that exceptional talent exists across the continent and will consider applications from suitably qualified candidates located within Africa who can support the regional travel requirements and responsibilities of the position. The Finance & Corporate Services Division is a strategic enabler of organisational performance, accountability and sustainability, delivering integrated services across Finance, Treasury, ERP & Digital Transformation, ICT, Supply Chain and Facilities. As part of an ambitious finance transformation programme, the division is strengthening financial governance, independent oversight, service excellence, and data-driven decision making across the organisation's global footprint. About the Role The Regional Finance Controller (RFC) is responsible for providing financial oversight, governance, assurance, compliance, and capacity building across Islamic Relief's country offices and implementing partners throughout West and East Africa. This is far more than a traditional financial control role. You will work closely with Country Directors, Finance Managers, operational teams, and local partners to strengthen financial management practices, build organisational capability, and ensure the highest standards of financial stewardship are embedded across the region. You will play a critical leadership role in improving financial performance, enhancing internal control frameworks, strengthening donor and statutory compliance, and supporting long-term financial sustainability. Through visible, hands-on engagement with country offices and partners, you will help drive a step-change in financial discipline, transparency, accountability, and decision-making. The role combines strategic oversight with practical delivery. You will be responsible for assessing financial performance, mentoring regional finance teams, identifying and mitigating risk, supporting fraud prevention initiatives, and ensuring finance effectively supports programme delivery and donor confidence. Reporting to the Global Finance Operations Lead, you will provide expert technical guidance and leadership across a diverse and complex regional portfolio, supporting the ongoing evolution of Islamic Relief's global finance operating model. The successful candidate will spend approximately 50% of their time travelling across the region, providing direct support to country offices, finance teams, and implementing partners. The Successful Candidate Will Have: A professionally recognised accounting qualification (ACCA, CIMA, ICAEW, ICMA or equivalent). Significant senior-level financial management experience, ideally within the humanitarian, NGO, development, or international non-profit sector. Demonstrable experience leading financial governance, compliance, assurance, and internal control activities across multiple entities or geographical locations. Strong expertise in budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling, financial planning, and scenario analysis. Experience producing consolidated management accounts, variance analysis, financial performance reporting, and strategic financial insight. Proven experience managing donor compliance requirements and statutory obligations. A strong understanding of financial risk management, fraud prevention, and control frameworks. Experience leading, developing, mentoring, and coaching finance teams. Excellent stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence and support both finance and non-finance leaders. Strong communication skills and the ability to present complex financial information clearly and effectively. Experience designing and delivering finance training, capability building, and development programmes. High levels of integrity, accountability, professionalism, and cultural sensitivity. Commitment to the mission, vision, and values of Islamic Relief Worldwide. Fluency in both English and French. Desirable Experience managing donor-funded programmes and institutional grant reporting within international NGOs. Experience working in fragile, conflict-affected, or complex operating environments. Strong understanding of the geopolitical, regulatory, and socio-economic contexts across Africa. Experience supporting finance transformation, organisational change, or continuous improvement initiatives. Experience working with local implementing partners and sub-grantees. Why Join Islamic Relief? This role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact across multiple countries by strengthening financial performance, governance, accountability, and sustainability throughout one of the world's leading humanitarian organisations. If you are a strategic finance leader who enjoys developing people, improving systems, driving compliance, and enabling operational excellence across international programmes, we would love to hear from you. For more information, please refer to the full Job Description and Person Specification. If you are talented, reliable, service-minded, resilient, and highly motivated, with a strong commitment to Islamic Relief's mission and values of Sincerity, Excellence, Compassion, Social Justice, and Custodianship, please submit your application via our online recruitment portal. PLEASE NOTE: Interviews may be held on an ongoing basis, and we reserve the right to close this vacancy prior to the advertised closing date should a suitable candidate be identified. Pre-Employment Checks Any employment with Islamic Relief will be subject to: Proof of eligibility to live and work within the UK. Satisfactory references. Appropriate screening and safeguarding checks. Please note that we are only able to consider applications from candidates who already have the right to work in the UK. Sponsorship is not available for this position. Our Values and Commitment to Safeguarding Islamic Relief is committed to preventing all forms of abuse, exploitation, harassment, discrimination, and financial misconduct. We expect all employees and volunteers to share this commitment and uphold the highest standards of conduct. All appointments are subject to satisfactory references and safeguarding checks, including participation in the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme where applicable. Islamic Relief is an equal opportunities employer.

How to Apply: **For further details about the role and application requirements, please refer to the full Job Description and Person Specification and apply via our online recruitment portal using the link below.** [**Regional Finance Controller**](https://islamic-relief.current-vacancies.com/Jobs/Advert/4327242?cid=1858&t=Regional-Finance-Controller)

We offer programs in 10 countries across Africa, Asia, the Middle East and North America, reaching millions of children each year in some of the most difficult places on earth, helping them to connect, learn and thrive. This work is supported by our two global offices in Toronto, Canada and London, UK; and seven National Offices in North America and Europe. Learn more about our programs in Ethiopia from our website . Oversees People & Culture processes to ensure compliance, best practices, and effective performance management, upholding strong DEIA standards, staff safety, and well-being. Demonstrates integrity and resilience, proactively addressing and mitigating legal risks, including seeking legal advice when necessary. 5.Information Requirement for Decision-Making: Makes decisions based on a combination of internal and external information, often requiring an analytic approach to draw conclusions from incomplete information or non-conclusive information. 6.Innovation and Improvements Drives innovation and continuous improvement to deliver high-quality, impactful programs and more efficient internal systems and ways of working. 7. Relationships & Communications: Internal / External: Builds and sustains strategic relationships with key stakeholders, including donors, government officials, UN agencies, academia, media, NGOs, and local partners, while promoting RTP’s identity and relevance to the needs of vulnerable populations, in alignment with the localization strategy. Leads strategic donor, HQ visits, workshops, represents RTP in high-level meetings, conferences, and media to strengthen its profile. 8. Expertise (Certifications / Education, Professional Experience): Extensive experience in leadership roles within a large or medium international development organization, including: strategic planning, leadership and people management, project management and planning, monitoring and evaluation and financial and risk management. Master’s degree in business administration, social sciences, development studies or related discipline. Experience working in or managing programmes in stable and fragile contexts. Proven success with mobilizing new sources of program funding. Understanding of laws, regulations and cultural dynamics local and international. Fluency in spoken and written Amharic and English Significant experience with a child-focused organization is desirable. 9.Core Competences: Collaboration: Highly collaborative with strong interpersonal skills; excels at working in with a multicultural team and builds rapport and trust to develop strong external partnerships. Growth Mindset: Demonstrates commitment to own professional development and encourages their team to develop their potential, creates a learning culture through effective coaching and mentorship. Communication: Communicates complex operational, technical & strategic issues clearly & credibly to diverse audiences, leveraging strong networks to secure donor funding & influence stakeholders. Resilience: Strong organizational skills and the ability to work under pressure: multi-tasking, meeting deadlines, solving problems creatively and embracing challenges with resilience. Professionalism: Models professionalism and RTP’s values, promoting a safe, inclusive workplace and positive impact for children and youth. Management and Interpersonal Skills : Lead and mentor country team with influence, fostering trust, high performance, and shared ownership of outcome. 10.Additional Information: Expected to travel regularly domestically and occasionally internationally and work outside regular hours.

En tant que membre de l’Équipe de direction de la Plateforme Afrique, vous piloterez l’engagement d’Oxfam auprès de l’Union africaine et de ses institutions. Vous élaborerez et mettrez en œuvre des stratégies de plaidoyer à fort impact afin d’influencer les politiques et les pratiques à l’échelle continentale. Vous représenterez Oxfam au plus haut niveau auprès de l’UA, nouerez des relations stratégiques et contribuerez à positionner Oxfam comme un partenaire crédible et de confiance. Ce poste joue un rôle central dans la réalisation de la mission d’Oxfam en Afrique : il établit un lien entre les espaces d’élaboration des politiques continentales et les réalités nationales, tout en veillant à ce que les actions de plaidoyer soient cohérentes, porteuses d’impact et ancrées dans les réalités vécues par les communautés. Ce poste relève de la Direction Afrique, avec un rattachement matriciel à la Direction Plaidoyer, Campagnes et Engagement (ACE). Profil recherché Nous recherchons une personne reconnue pour son leadership en matière de plaidoyer et d’influence, disposant d’une solide expérience de collaboration avec l’Union africaine ou des institutions multilatérales comparables. Vous avez démontré votre capacité à concevoir et à mettre en œuvre des stratégies d’influence porteuses d’impact, combinant analyse des politiques, plaidoyer, communication médiatique et partenariats afin de favoriser des changements significatifs. Vous excellez dans l’établissement de relations et la négociation, savez évoluer efficacement dans des environnements complexes associant de multiples parties prenantes et êtes en mesure d’exercer une influence au plus haut niveau. Grâce à votre capacité de réflexion stratégique et d’analyse politique, vous savez traduire les processus de l’UA en possibilités concrètes d’influence et d’impact pour les pays et les partenaires. Votre expérience du leadership vous permet de diriger des équipes diversifiées et de travailler au sein d’un réseau mondial, tout en favorisant la collaboration et la redevabilité. Vous avez une connaissance approfondie du contexte sociopolitique africain et adhérez aux approches féministes, décoloniales et portées par les partenaires. La maîtrise professionnelle de l’anglais et du français est indispensable. Pourquoi nous rejoindre Ce poste offre une occasion rare d’influencer les politiques et les pratiques au plus haut niveau continental. À Oxfam, vous façonnerez notre engagement auprès de l’Union africaine, piloterez le plaidoyer sur des enjeux majeurs tels que les inégalités, la pauvreté et la justice, et collaborerez avec des gouvernements, des diplomates et des institutions internationales pour réaliser des changements concrets. Au sein d’une équipe de direction diversifiée et collaborative, vous contribuerez à rapprocher les politiques continentales des réalités des communautés, afin que les décisions prises au plus haut niveau se traduisent par des résultats tangibles pour les populations partout en Afrique. Ce que nous offrons À Oxfam, nous sommes convaincus que chaque aspect de notre travail peut contribuer à un changement positif. Si vous partagez cette conviction et possédez les compétences nécessaires pour relever les défis liés à ce poste, cette fonction vous offrira de grandes possibilités d’épanouissement personnel ainsi que d’excellentes perspectives d’évolution professionnelle. Oxfam s’engage à proposer une rémunération équitable, sur la base d’une semaine de travail de 36 heures À propos de nous Oxfam est un mouvement mondial de personnes qui agissent ensemble pour mettre fin à l’injustice qu’est la pauvreté. Cela signifie que nous nous attaquons aux inégalités qui maintiennent les populations dans la pauvreté. Ensemble, nous sauvons des vies, protégeons les populations et les aidons à reconstruire leur existence. Lorsqu’une catastrophe survient, nous aidons les personnes à bâtir un avenir meilleur, pour elles-mêmes et pour les autres. Nous agissons sur des enjeux tels que les droits fonciers, le changement climatique et les discriminations à l’égard des femmes. Et nous ne nous arrêterons pas tant que chaque personne sur la planète ne pourra pas vivre à l’abri de la pauvreté. Nous sommes une confédération internationale composée de 22 organisations affiliées et du Secrétariat d’Oxfam International. Avec nos partenaires et les communautés locales, nous menons des actions humanitaires, des programmes de développement et des campagnes dans plus de 76 pays. Oxfam en Afrique (OiA) est une plateforme continentale qui assure la coordination des bureaux pays d’Oxfam en Afrique et collabore avec des organisations de la société civile, des universitaires, des gouvernements et le secteur privé afin de contribuer à une Afrique plus égalitaire, en remettant en cause les structures de pouvoir qui perpétuent les inégalités et les injustices. À cette fin, Oxfam en Afrique apporte un leadership intellectuel dynamique et offre un espace de collaboration à ses partenaires. Oxfam en Afrique joue un rôle moteur dans l’appui aux communautés locales et le renforcement de leur pouvoir d’agir, la promotion de l’égalité de genre, le plaidoyer en faveur de changements de politiques publiques et le renforcement des capacités des organisations locales de la société civile. L’ensemble de notre travail est guidé par nos valeurs fondamentales : Autonomisation, Redevabilité, Inclusion, Courage, Solidarité et Égalité. Notre engagement en matière de safeguarding (Protection contre le harcèlement, l’exploitation et les abus sexuels) Oxfam s’engage à prévenir toute forme de comportement inapproprié au travail, notamment le harcèlement sexuel, l’exploitation et les abus sexuels, les manquements à l’intégrité et les irrégularités financières, ainsi qu’à promouvoir le bien-être des enfants, des jeunes et des adultes. Oxfam attend de l’ensemble de son personnel et de ses volontaires qu’ils partagent cet engagement et respectent notre Code de conduite. Nous accordons une importance primordiale au recrutement de personnes qui partagent nos valeurs et les mettent en pratique. Remarque : Toute offre d’emploi sera subordonnée à la réception de références satisfaisantes et pourra faire l’objet de contrôles appropriés, notamment une vérification du casier judiciaire et des contrôles relatifs au financement du terrorisme. Le Secrétariat d’Oxfam International participe également au Mécanisme interorganisations de divulgation des inconduites (Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme). Conformément à ce dispositif, si une personne candidate a précédemment travaillé pour une autre organisation membre, nous solliciterons auprès de cette organisation des informations concernant toute constatation d’exploitation sexuelle, d’abus sexuels et/ou de harcèlement sexuel survenue pendant son emploi, ainsi que tout incident qui faisait encore l’objet d’une enquête au moment de son départ. En soumettant sa candidature, la personne candidate confirme avoir pris connaissance de cette procédure de recrutement.

EMERGENCY is an independent and neutral international organisation founded in 1994 to provide free, high-quality medical and surgical care to victims of war, landmines and poverty. Through partnership and collaborations, we work to ensure the inclusion of older people across society and strive to deliver a just and fair world for everyone as they get older. As countries prepare for and adapt to population ageing, we are seeking to make a difference at a critical juncture to how societies, economies and institutions adapt to this change. Gather stories, case studies and learning content from network members and partners across Africa. Develop communications and visibility materials that strengthen member engagement and showcase network impact across the region, including ensuring up-to-date information in digital and website platforms. Maintain regional communications channels including social media pages and support knowledge sharing within Africa and across the wider HelpAge network. description:
HEAD OF NETWORK DEVELOPMENT Location Global, whereHelpAge can currently employ: Ethiopia, India, Italy, Jordan, Kenya, Nepal, Pakistan, Spain, Tanzania, Thailand, Turkey, United Kingdom or Zimbabwe, with a preference for candidates based in the Global South. Department Network Development Reports to (Line Manager) Director of Global Impact Responsible for (Line managing) Regional Advisers (4) Network SupportLead Humanitarian Capacity Strengthening Manager ( SHAPE ) Network Platform Manager SCORE Programme Manager Indirectly responsible for Country Director – Ukraine (viathe Network Support Lead) Grade F Contract Type Full time equivalent /Open-ended contract About HelpAge HelpAge International works with a diverse global network of around 200 organisations across 99 countries to promote the rights of older people to lead dignified, healthy and secure lives. Through partnership and collaborations, we work to ensure the inclusion of older people across society and strive to deliver a just and fair world for everyone as they get older. Our work is driven by our desire to achieve real impact for older people, to be inclusive, to work in partnership and to learn from our shared experience. As countries prepare for and adapt to population ageing, we are seeking to make a difference at a critical juncture to how societies, economies and institutions adapt to this change. Our Strategy 2030, Ageing in a Just World, sets out how we will work to shape the future we all share. By working together with our partners, we aim to inspire a movement for change. By ensuring all our work promotes older people’s wellbeing, dignity and voice, we seek to transform the lives of older people now and in the future. Guided by our commitment to our values of impact, learning, partnership, and inclusion, we partner with others to bring systemic change and impact at scale. By acting as a supporter, convenor and thought leader, we want to make an impact that matters for older people and their communities. Our organisational culture The culture of the organisation aims to ensure: Accountability for All: Every individual and team member is responsible for their actions and decisions, ensuring alignment with organisational priorities and commitments to partners and network members. Trust, Respect, and Inclusion: We strive to create an environment where mutual trust is the foundation of all relationships, diverse perspectives are valued, and everyone feels included in decision-making processes. Culture of Collaboration: Working together across teams, network members, and partners to share knowledge, maximise impact, and drive collective success, rather than working in silos. Openness and Transparency: Ensuring open communication, clear decision-making processes and actions, and a commitment to sharing information in a way that builds trust and accountability. Collective Responsibilities Within and With Partners and Network: Recognising that achieving our mission requires shared responsibility, we promote joint ownership of decisions, initiatives, and outcomes across HelpAge and its network members and partners. Staff and network members are valued: Staff and network members are recognised, and valued and appreciated for their contributions, fostering an environment where every individual feels respected, supported, and integral to our mission, with their input and expertise recognised as vital to achieving our shared goals. The Behavioural competencies outlined below support this culture. About the Department The Global Impact Team drives HelpAge International’s mission to advance the wellbeing, dignity, and rights of older people, by championing locally led action and global solidarity. At the heart of our work is a thriving, resilient HelpAge global network—a powerful collective of national civil society actors driving change that is rooted in the priorities and experiences of older people. We lead the delivery of HelpAge’s strategic approach to support, convene, and influence, across humanitarian and development contexts, to achieve lasting and inclusive impact. Our goal is to ensure that: Older people have inclusive, improved access to secure and adequate income Older people have safe and secure access to humanitarian assistance Older people have improved access to inclusive health, care, and support services Age-inclusive laws, policies and systems guarantee older people’s rights across all sectors A thriving locally led HelpAge Network drives collective action to uphold older people’s rights, dignity, and wellbeing. About the Job The Head of Network Development will provide strategic leadership for HelpAge International's global network engagement and development, localisation, and capacity strengthening work - advancing our commitment to locally led action and building strong, values-driven relationships with network members and other strategic partners. This role will lead and be accountable for the development and delivery of the HelpAge network strategy, ensuring alignment with our global mission and enabling inclusive, sustainable collaboration across the HelpAge network. The postholder provides strategic leadership for network engagement, development and capacity strengthening across all regions - Africa, Asia, Eurasia and the Middle East, Europe, and Latin America and the Caribbean. They lead through the Regional Advisers rather than delivering regional workstreams personally: setting annual priorities and deliverables for each region, in alignment with organisational priorities, and hold Regional Advisers accountable for delivery through regular performance management and review. This is an evolving role. The postholder ensures the capacity strengthening and localisation offer is shaped by what members themselves identify as their needs and differentiated by region and member segment, rather than applied uniformly. They lead the mechanisms that connect global and regional levels of the network - regional convenings, member-to-member exchange, and the flow of regional intelligence into global strategy, positioning and funding decisions. The role works in close partnership with internal stakeholders - Executive Leadership Group, Board, Leadership Group, and Team Heads - and external stakeholders including network members, civil society organisations, local consortia, donors, and institutional partners. The postholder leads the preparation and quality of Governance Committee submissions and Board papers on network development and engagement. Alongside this regional remit, the role holder will lead directly on coordinating members in the Europe region, and work closely with the Head of Advocacy and Evidencing to develop our strategic niche on donor advocacy in Europe. Key areas for impact/influence and responsibilities To make an impact and influence, the role holder will shape and deliver the HelpAge network strategy and HelpAge's transition to locally led ways of working; provide strategic oversight of network member engagement, localisation, and the organisational capacity sharing strategy; lead HelpAge's support to country transitions, including Ukraine; and build an inclusive, resilient and effective global network of local and national organisations. Network strategy and impact Lead delivery of the HelpAge network strategy, ensuring it supports locally led transitions, strong partnerships and member engagement. Lead the Thriving Network Impact Vehicle (one of six priority areas through which HelpAge delivers its strategy; the other five target external policy change - social pensions, health coverage, humanitarian action, legal rights, climate adaptation - while this one targets the health and sustainability of the network itself) and its results framework, ensuring a clear connection between day-to-day activities and HelpAge's 2030 network targets, and reporting quarterly to the senior leadership team on progress. Hold direct responsibility for engagement with Europe-based members, and work with the Head of Advocacy and Evidencing to develop HelpAge's strategic niche on donor advocacy in Europe. Set the strategic frame for network convenings - purpose, frequency, participant profile and hold Regional Advisers accountable for regional and thematic convenings. Chair the strategic reference group INDABA, HelpAge's consultative forum with network members. Lead delivery of the Network Capacity Sharing Strategy, translating it into a coherent network-wide offer, integrated across programmes, in collaboration with Programme Support, Advocacy and Evidencing and other relevant teams. About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. In Ethiopia, we engage farmers in agroforestry and community-based seed multiplication to increase farmers’ incomes and make farming systems more resilient. Engaging with local actors at every step but bringing innovative ideas from outside, we are making rural farming more market-friendly and environmentally sustainable. The farmers we work with in Ethiopia have planted more than 30 million trees, produced over 1500 metric tonnes of improved teff seed, and improved the futures of nearly 200,000 community members. Our permanent team numbers over 180 with nearly 1,000 rural seasonal staff supporting them. Our country headquarters are in Addis Ababa and we have a large program office in Bahir Dar, plus several smaller field offices. The role synthesizes geographic, agricultural, environmental, market, and stakeholder information to support strategic expansion decisions and operational readiness. The officer will participate in field scouting visits with the expansion team to validate desk research findings and gather additional insights. Collect, analyze, and synthesize agricultural, environmental, demographic, socioeconomic, market, and government data to support expansion planning. Review secondary data from government institutions, research organizations, development partners, and other credible sources to generate evidence-based insights. Monitor demographic, agricultural, environmental, market, and policy trends to identify opportunities and potential risks for program expansion. Develop and maintain databases, trackers, and research documentation to support expansion planning and operational readiness. Verify, clean, and analyze research and field data to ensure quality, accuracy, consistency, and usability. Support the development and continuous improvement of expansion assessment tools, scoring frameworks, research methodologies, and analytical processes. Field & Stakeholder Verification of Data Participate in field scouting and assessment visits to validate desk research findings and collect additional information. Engage with government offices, development partners, local stakeholders, and other relevant actors to verify data, assumptions, and findings. Assess key expansion criteria, including agroforestry suitability, water availability, land suitability, market potential, operational feasibility, scalability, accessibility, and implementation risks. Identify data gaps and discrepancies and coordinate with relevant stakeholders to obtain and validate additional information. Integrate field observations and stakeholder feedback with secondary data to strengthen expansion assessments and recommendations. Reporting & Collaboration Prepare clear and evidence-based assessment reports, analytical summaries, and recommendations to support expansion decisions. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to translate research findings and stakeholder insights into actionable recommendations and expansion plans. Support the recruitment of field staff Career Growth and Development We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. Terms of Reference for IUCN Consultancy Title: Provision of Vehicle Rental Services Objective of the Consultancy This consultancy has the following objective: 1. To secure reliable transportation services for staff coordinating and supporting the implementation of the NbS4Water Africa – Ethiopia Awash Project Background Project Reference: - Donor reference: DN01983 About IUCN IUCN is a membership Union uniquely composed of both government and civil society organisations. It provides public, private and non-governmental organisations with the knowledge and tools that enable human progress, economic development and nature conservation to take place together. Created in 1948, IUCN is now the world’s largest and most diverse environmental network, harnessing the knowledge, resources and reach of more than 1,400 Member organisations and around 15,000 experts. It is a leading provider of conservation data, assessments and analysis. Its broad membership enables IUCN to fill the role of incubator and trusted repository of best practices, tools and international standards. IUCN provides a neutral space in which diverse stakeholders including governments, NGOs, scientists, businesses, local communities, indigenous peoples organisations and others can work together to forge and implement solutions to environmental challenges and achieve sustainable development. Working with many partners and supporters, IUCN implements a large and diverse portfolio of conservation projects worldwide. Combining the latest science with the traditional knowledge of local communities, these projects work to reverse habitat loss, restore ecosystems and improve people’s well-being. www.iucn.org https://twitter.com/IUCN/ About the Project The project focuses on promoting catchment protection through Nature-based Solutions (NbS), framed as best adaptive practices in the context of climate change and increasing land degradation. It aims to scale up NbS for watershed restoration in alignment with national basin development, land degradation neutrality, and landscape restoration goals. The general objective is to enhance water-related ecosystem services in key watersheds of the Awash sub-basin for the benefit of both people and the environment through the application of NbS. To achieve this, the project will strengthen action-oriented partnerships among community-based organizations (CBOs), the wider public, national and local governments, and non-government actors. These partnerships will promote NbS that build knowledge, shape positive attitudes, and encourage good practices, mobilizing society as a whole to achieve large-scale watershed rehabilitation, restoration, and sustainable development and use. The general objective of the project is to improve ground water recharge of the little Akaki catchment of the upper Awash river basin focusing on Guleel & Addis Ketema sub-cities of Addis Ababa and Sululta town of Sheger city, specifically in Bilisuma micro catchment. Description of the Assignment The overall objective of this procurement is to competitively select and contract qualified vehicle rental or leasing service provider(s) capable of providing reliable, safe, well-maintained, and appropriately insured vehicles to support the implementation of the NbS4Water Africa – Ethiopia Awash Project. Maintain professional conduct when interacting with IUCN staff, partners, consultants, and other passengers. 3. The CSD also works closely with DCD-P and Programme and Project Managers. At headquarters (HQ) level, apart from the RHoSO, her/his counterparts on the methodological level are Regional Logistic Coordinator, Regional HR Coordinator, Finance coordinator, RDD Logistics & Procurement Department, RDD HR Department as well as the Compliance department. Main Duties and Responsibilities: Strategic Leadership The CSD assists the CD in the management of the country programme, participates in the senior management meetings, and pro-actively takes part in the decision-making processes; Ensures that systems and operations support the implementation of the country programme strategy and that procedures and regulations are implemented in full transparency and in accordance with donor and PIN rules; represents PIN towards local authorities, donors, partners, and other stakeholders; is responsible for adequate staffing of all supervised departments in order to achieve efficient delivery of People in Need’s (PIN) country programme; promotes team spirit, a culture of respect, personal responsibility, transparency, and openness; ensures and promote efficient communication and information sharing among operations and program teams. Finance & Accounting Oversee Finance team while ensuring they have sufficient capacity both in number and qualification and securing their continuous capacity building based on personal development plans; The CSD makes sure that relevant country programme financial and administrative procedures are in place and respected; Ensures financial and administrative systems (ELO, Navision) are properly administrated and used by the whole country programme; In cooperation with the financial team guarantees that financial requirements are met in all sectors, including budgeting, reporting and accounting of the country programme; Optimizes financial resources allocation to cover operations costs; monitors and notifies HQ about crucial operations costs misbalance as compared to the total country programme budget; In cooperation with Head of Finance, prepares financial and economic overviews and interprets economic data for country programme and programme management teams; Supervise the Head of Finance and Project Managers and provides methodological support during the new project budgeting process; Supervise the Head of Finance and Project Managers and provides methodological support during project budget spending monitoring and planning process; Supervises the financial aspects of partner selection and assessment processes, partnership agreement preparation, capacity building and reporting; CSD is involved in negotiation and establishing partnership with implementing partners (INGOs and national NGOs), drafts the relevant provision to partnership and implementing agreements, based on the assessment of partners´ capacities, PIN procedures and donor´s compliance requirement Supervise and support the Head of Finance during audits Supervise and support the Head of Finance during annual accounting closing Is responsible for preparation and monitoring CP Operational Budget Procurement Oversee and lead the Procurement team; Ensure the CP Procurement Guidelines are updated and respected Oversee and implement the procurement system, following all relevant donor and PIN guidelines and procedures, and considering relevant corruption risks; Ensure that the Annual Procurement Plans are in place and regularly updated; On a regular basis audit the procurement process in order to highlight flaws and pressures associated with operating in the Country Programme context; Logistics Oversee the Logistic team while ensuring they have sufficient capacity both in number and qualification and securing their continuous capacity building based on personal development plans; Implement and/or strengthen systems of oversight and prevention of corruption; Oversee Logistics budgets and contribute to planning needs for new projects with regards to security and logistics; Supervise functioning of asset registry and inventory control; Supervise and support Head of Operations during yearly inventories; Ensure efficient tools for fleet planning and costs monitoring are in place and efficiently used Human Resources and Capacity Development Oversee the HR team while ensuring they have sufficient capacity both in number and qualification and securing their continuous capacity building based on personal development plans The CSD is familiar with PIN HR procedures and ensures that all country programme staff follows them; Makes sure that relevant country programme HR procedures are in place and respected, and updates them on regular basis; Supervises the process of internal and external recruitment of national staff; Ensure that system of in-country induction for both international and national staff is in place; Ensures that regular staff evaluation is in place and that bonuses and capacity development tools are being used according to HR guidelines; Ensures that the contract termination procedures are followed properly; Ensure that all HR administration systems for country programme are operating properly, in particular overseeing the proper implementation of administrative issues related to HR; Together with the country programme senior management and national HR personnel, cooperate with HQ HR department on HR audits, setting and improving of HR procedures, and supporting their implementation; Together with the national HR personnel, inform HQ HR about current HR related needs and requests from country programmes Proactive identification and response to staff concerns, working with the ETHHR team in identifying and understanding satisfaction/interpersonal issues and how to effectively address them Responsible for consulting and providing guidance on the revision of staff salaries and the ETH salary scale Responsible for establishing succession plans for key roles, helping to identify high potential staff members, and establishing development plans for key individuals and the ETH HR team External and Internal Compliance The CSD ensures that all taxes are paid in line with national regulatory framework; Ensures that tax exemption (when possible) will be applied by NGO; In coordination with the CD, ensures that all agenda related to permits, licences, and registrations are dealt with as and when required. Ensures the current contract templates on the country programme are up to date and properly used; Conducts regular checks on proper archiving of finance, procurement and HR documents; Is familiar with donors’ conditions in finance, logistics and procurement and requirements and makes sure they are respected; Acts as a communication channel between donors in case of any requests related to the compliance in HR or procurement field And fulfils any other tasks as required. Main Requirements: University degree preferably in Finance/Economics, Logistic, Public Administration, Law or related field; Significant previous experience with managing systems, finance, procurement, administration and HR; Ability to work closely with senior management (Country Director and Head of Programmes) to share the strategic direction of the country programme, ensuring that systems support programme implementation; Experience with financial management, including budgeting, financial reporting and compliance with donor regulations; Knowledge of logistics and procurement processes, including asset management, fleet planning, and procurement systems that comply with donor regulations; Experience in overseeing HR functions, including capacity building, staff evaluations, and salary scale management, ensuring compliance with national regulations and organizational policies; Ability to develop teams across logistics, procurement, finance, and HR; Strong problem-solving skills; Excellent communication skills, including fluent spoken and written English; IT literacy, advanced knowledge of MS Excel, working experience with accounting and economic software; We offer: Working environment in a well-established humanitarian organization in a challenging context Salary & Benefits : Salary based on PIN’s salary scale and HR policies; expected salary range between 3250 - 3600 EUR super gross (based on experience) Additional allowances include : Monthly Subsistence Allowance of 1440 EUR Housing Allowance/Accommodation in PIN guesthouse Time off and Rest: 25 days of holiday annually 10 sick days Travel benefits: Reimbursement of travel expenses with travel to the country of residence once every 6 months of work Reimbursement of costs of visas and vaccinations; assistance with the visa application procedure Reimbursement for the medical check-up before and after the deployment Travel health insurance covering medical care, incl. the repatriation Health and Well-being: 24/7 Medical Support available online Free psychological consultations available online Professional Development: Free access to e-learning platforms and PIN Learning Hub; title: Government Relations Advisor, Africa
description:
PLEASE NOTE: This search is being conducted by Ethiojobs. Please apply DIRECTLY through the link below : https://ethiojobs.net/job/UAVcbgg81M-government-relations-advisor-africa-vital-strategies _________________ Vital Strategies is an international public health organization. Our programs strengthen public health systems and address the world’s leading causes of illness, injury and death. We currently work in 73 countries, supporting data-driven decision making in government, advancing evidence-based public health policies, and mounting strategic communication campaigns. Vital Strategies’ priorities are driven by the greatest potential to improve and save lives. They include non-communicable disease prevention, tobacco control, road safety, obesity prevention, overdose prevention, environmental health, and vital statistics systems building. Our programs are primarily concentrated in low- and middle-income countries in Africa, Latin America, Asia and the Pacific. Please visit our website at www.vitalstrategies.org to find out more about our work. Vital Strategies is committed to building a diverse, equitable and inclusive (DEI) organization. We believe our programs are strengthened when they are developed and supported by individuals with diverse life experiences, whose understanding of social and cultural issues can help make our work and workforce more inclusive. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. Lead Poisoning Prevention Program: Vital Strategies is expanding our program that addresses the issue of lead poisoning in low- and middle-income countries. We plan to build upon existing efforts and interest by collaborating with governmental agencies in countries in Africa, Asia, and Latin America to strengthen health systems and build local expertise in childhood lead exposure to enact sound, cost-effective policies to address exposures. Job Purpose: The position of Government Relations Advisor, Africa will facilitate regional exchange and coordinate high-level engagement and partnership building for the Lead Poisoning Prevention Program across multiple countries in Africa. The role will focus on managing and strengthening relationships with key government and program partners, stakeholders, facilitating regional exchanges and strategy development, and ensuring program alignment with countries’ priorities and global objectives. The incumbent will work closely with country teams to support government engagement, partnership building, share updates on implementation progress, and ensure exchange and coordination among government and consortium partners across the regional portfolio. The role will also provide representation at regional events, support policy engagement, and ensure effective collaboration among regional stakeholders and technical partners. It is preferred that this role be based in Ethiopia, on a full-time hybrid schedule, out of Vital Strategies' office in Addis Ababa, but we are also open to qualified candidates from Ghana, Rwanda, and Tanzania. The candidate must have authorization to work legally in the respective country at the time of hire. Vital Strategies offers highly competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits. The salary range for this position will vary by location, experience and qualifications. Duties and Responsibilities: Regional program coordination and strategic vision - · In coordination with the global team, facilitate regional exchanges and development of regional partnerships and a consistent strategy for government engagement and partnership building in the region; · Initiate and/or sustain government partnerships with ministries, regulatory bodies, and other national and regional institutions in priority countries; · Support project launches and startups in new countries within the region, including support for staff recruitment; · Support country teams in translating strategy into implementation plans, including identification of key capacity gaps to be filled, and government engagement needed to ensure quality and timely delivery of program activities; · Identify and participate in regional opportunities and events that help elevate lead poisoning on national agendas; · Promote multisectoral collaboration and partnership-driven approaches to environmental health policy development; · Manage relationships with regional organizations engaged in lead-related activities, and develop, where appropriate, formal or contractual relationships for discrete programmatic activities in support of the initiative. Partnership Management - · Support country teams in managing key government and institutional partners across the region, as well as non-government organizations in relevant sectors; · Represent Vital Strategies in regional lead poisoning prevention meetings, technical forums, public hearings, and governance bodies in the region; · Support the development and review of reports, policy briefs, and training materials developed in the region; · Promote cross-sector dialogues that support the development of integrated, evidence-based public policies; · Facilitate knowledge exchange across the region; · Coordinate work with national and international partners, ensuring alignment across local and global strategies; · Assist with other duties as specified by the supervisor. Qualifications: Education & Degree - · Master’s degree in public health, public policy/Administration, Global Health, international development, environmental health science, or related field. Skills & Abilities - · Strong government engagement and partnership-building skills, with the ability to establish and sustain relationships with ministries, regulatory bodies, and regional institutions; · Demonstrated ability to coordinate multi-country initiatives and facilitate regional exchange and collaboration; · Strategic thinking skills, with the ability to translate regional strategy into actionable country-level implementation plans; · Strong stakeholder management skills across government, NGOs, multilateral agencies, and technical partners; · Ability to promote and facilitate multisectoral collaboration and policy dialogue; · Ability to monitor program quality, performance, and outcomes across a regional portfolio; · Ability to coordinate and engage program stakeholders and other country teams; · Demonstrated sensitivity in handling confidential information; · Proven ability to interpret public health data, generate actionable insights, and support policy recommendations; · Exhibits strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple competing priorities and meet deadlines; demonstrates personal integrity, credibility, and professionalism while taking initiative and making sound, informed decisions in a fast-paced environment; · Professional oral and written proficiency in English; · Excellent interpersonal skills, including the ability to communicate effectively to technical and non-technical audiences, and contribute to an interdisciplinary international team; · Solid knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook); · Experience working with a geographically distributed team with demonstrated ability to work collaboratively, communicate clearly and regularly, monitor performance, and inspire, engage, and motivate staff; · Demonstrated commitment to contributing to an inclusive working and learning environment. Experience: Required - · Minimum of eight years of experience in government engagement and public health programming, ideally with experience in health policy, environmental health, and/or global health, especially related to lead poisoning prevention or environmental pollution; · Experience in representing organizations with governments, international institutions, and senior stakeholder forums; · Experience managing multi-country programs in Africa; · Experience working with government agencies, regulatory bodies, and public health facilities; · Experience with program reporting and monitoring. Preferred - · Demonstrated experience in communicating scientific and health information to varied audiences; · Experience in using project management platforms. Working Conditions and Physical Requirements: · If hired in Ghana, Rwanda, or Tanzania, the candidate will be hired via Vital Strategies’ Employer of Record on a remote schedule; · The position will require travel up to 30% of the time to visit operating countries in the region to visit field implementation or attend meetings with partners; · The candidate needs to be willing to work with colleagues across different time zones.
